items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that we want to solve the quadratic equation

Content:
[MATH: x^2+5x+6=0.]

Content:
The square root method won't work here, since there is a linear term. We can't factor out the variable, either, since there is a constant term. So, what should we do?

Content:
One way to solve this is to factor the entire trinomial on the left-hand side. To do this, we need to find two numbers that

Content:
- multiply to give [MATH: 6] (the constant term) and
- add to give [MATH: 5] (the linear coefficient).

Content:
These two numbers are [MATH: 2] and [MATH: 3.] So, we can factor the left-hand-side as follows:
[MATH: x^{2} + 5x + 6|= 0; x^{2} + 2x + 3x_(⏟)_(5x) + 6|= 0; (x^{2} + 2x) + (3x + 6)|= 0; x(x + 2) + 3(x + 2)|= 0; (x + 3)(x + 2)|= 0]

Content:
Applying the zero product rule, we have

Content:
[MATH: x+3=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x+2=0,]

Content:
which in turn gives

Content:
[MATH: x=-3 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=-2.]

Content:
Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=-3,-2.]

sections.normalized_html:
We will factor the left-hand side and then apply the zero product rule.

To factor the left-hand side, we need to find two numbers that multiply to [MATH: 6] and add to [MATH: -5.] These two numbers are [MATH: -2] and [MATH: -3,] so we can factor the left-hand side as follows:

[MATH: \eqalign{ x^2 - 5x + 6 &= 0 \[5pt] x^2 \underbrace{-3x -2x}_{\large -5x} + 6 &= 0 \[5pt] x(x-3) - 2(x-3) &= 0 \[5pt] (x - 2)(x -3) &= 0 }]

Applying the zero product rule, we have

[MATH: x-2=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x-3=0,]

which in turn gives

[MATH: x=2 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=3.]

Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=2,3.]

To factor the equation, we need two numbers that multiply to [MATH: 9] and add to [MATH: 10.] These two numbers are [MATH: 1] and [MATH: 9,] so we can factor the left-hand side as follows:

[MATH: x^{2} + 10x + 9|= 0; x^{2} + (1x + 9x) + 9|= 0; (x^{2} + x) + (9x + 9)|= 0; x(x + 1) + 9(x + 1)|= 0; (x + 9)(x + 1)|= 0]

Applying the zero product rule, we have

[MATH: x+9=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x+1=0,]

which in turn gives

[MATH: x=-9 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=-1.]

Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=-9,-1.]
